```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 18_regression_first_guess
title: Make a guess
questions:
  - id: unknown_coffee
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    answerLabel: Example answer
    prompt: >
      Say we don't know how much coffee the new student drank. What test score would you
      guess they'll get? What made you pick that score?
    answer: >
      I'd start with 70, the average for the seven students we've seen so far. That's my
      best guess before I know anything about this particular student.

  - id: average_coffee
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    answerLabel: Example answer
    prompt: >
      Now suppose the new student tells you they drank exactly one cup of coffee, the
      average amount for our sample so far. What would you guess now?
    answer: >
      The one student who drank exactly one cup scored 65, so I can see a case for 65.
      Or you might stick with 70. One cup puts our new student right in the middle of
      the scatterplot, where the two mean lines meet.

  - id: more_coffee
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    answerLabel: Example answer
    prompt: >
      Now say they drank a cup and a half, more than average. Would you change your
      guess? What do you see in the scatterplot that makes you think so?
    answer: >
      I'd lean toward a lower score. The points tend to slope downward as I look from
      left to right. That gives me a direction to go in, but it still leaves me with the
      question of how far to go.

  - id: precise_guess
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    answerLabel: Example answer
    prompt: >
      If you had to put a number on it, what score would you predict for a student who
      drank a cup and a half? What about a student who drank no coffee? How did you
      decide?
    answer: >
      At a cup and a half I see a 50 and a 65, so I might guess halfway between them. At
      zero cups there's just one student. Do I go with their 90? Or do I step back and
      use the pattern across all seven students to make both guesses?
```
